real_defects.issue: compareCsv wrote activity names, constraint text and other cells from the contractor's XER with no formula-injection guard, so a task name like =HYPERLINK(...) ran when the owner's rep opened the 'update changes' CSV. platform/ci/check_csv_formula_guard.py exits 1 on main since #17621 (it runs as an unwired check in ventures-tests). Fixed: cells starting = + - @ tab CR get an apostrophe unless a plain number; CR also forces quoting. The same one-line guard also landed concurrently in #17625 (hearth-and-horizon run, which saw main's guard red); this PR keeps that guard, adds CR quoting and the failing-first test.

In a multi-project XER the page passed only curProjId, so the previous file fell back to the project with the most open activities: picking OFFICE-FITOUT compared it with OTHER and reported all 22 activities added and 46 deleted. Fixed: the previous project is matched by proj_short_name, then proj_id (matchingProject).

--project was ignored with --previous (compare mode), so the CLI compared whichever project had the most open work. Fixed: --project picks the project by ID in both files and exits 2 when either lacks it.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
